body: Forward test of the promise-tracker credibility method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.62 (naive base rate 0.45) that: ICICI Bank reports a higher net interest margin for Q4 FY27 than for Q3 FY27. Evidence: Q2 FY27 call (Oct-2026): NIM 4.18% vs 4.36% in Q1 (4.28% ex tax-refund interest); drag from ~$18 bn FCNR(B) deposits under the RBI swap window and lower CASA (9–10 bp mix impact). CFO Sandeep Batra: 'The full impact would largely get reflected in the third quarter, after which we expect the margins to start moving up, even based on the current level of policy rates'; 'when repo repricing happens, there is a positive movement on the NIM… repo rates can go up to 6%… another two hikes'. Loans +30% YoY (24% ex FCNR-funded), deposits +27%, provisions ₹851 cr (0.2% of advances). Reasoning: This is a dated, specific promise (margins trough in Q3, rise thereafter) from a bank whose margin guidance has generally been reliable, and the rate-hike cycle reprices ICICI's large repo-linked book faster than deposits. Risks: deposit repricing and FCNR deployment. Above base. Resolution: YES if the net interest margin ICICI Bank reports for Q4 FY27 (Jan–Mar 2027) in its Q4 results/presentation is strictly greater than the NIM it reports for Q3 FY27 (as stated in the Q3 release, both on the bank's headline basis). Equal = NO. Source: ICICI Bank Q3 and Q4 FY27 results press releases / investor presentations (NSE). Resolve by 2027-05-15; score with Brier vs base rate.

data.base_rate_reasoning: Indian large private banks report a sequential NIM increase in roughly 45% of quarters (flat or down otherwise).
